experiment_name: ASU-independent self-play training-plumbing smoke (3 games, 1 train_step)

algorithm_config.component: MonopolyZeroNet + MaxNPUCT/SearchAdapter + arena.play_game + ReplayBuffer + train_step (never Trainer/population_jobs)

result: Training plumbing verified end to end with zero ASU involvement: 3 short games all completed (0 illegal actions, 0 crashes), 721 positions collected and accepted into a fresh ReplayBuffer with none rejected, one train_step update produced a finite loss and changed all 16/16 model parameter tensors (confirmed via torch.equal against pre-update clones, not just one). Goal was plumbing, not strength - no claim about policy quality is made.
notes: integrity.fallbacks is null, not 0: this smoke's vs_fixed game used monopoly_bench.adapters.FixedAdapter, whose internal compatibility_fallbacks counter is never surfaced into arena.play_game's GameResult.fallbacks (FixedAdapter.choose_action always returns ActionDecision with the default fallback=False even when it substitutes an illegal action), and the script does not read FixedAdapter.compatibility_fallbacks directly - so whether any fallback substitutions happened during the vs_fixed game genuinely was not captured, and is not assumed to be zero. A second run of this same script (not saved as an artifact) produced similar but not byte-identical numbers (721 vs. 697 positions) - expected, since self_play=True deliberately injects exploration randomness (temperature/Dirichlet noise) as part of MaxNPUCT's designed self-play behavior, distinct from the PYTHONHASHSEED reproducibility finding documented elsewhere.
